props.title: Two Centuries of Colonies — Now Arguing With London
props.subline: 1763: Three boxes — end of salutary neglect, Proclamation Line, Pontiac's Rebellion

props.title: Britain Won the Biggest War — and Broke the System
nodes: War leaves London drowning in debt — books' word is 'enormous'
Empire costs more than ever: Canada to garrison, Florida to administer, frontier past every map London owned
Thesis: Britain won the war and wrecked the arrangement that had made the empire work

props.title: George Grenville — Prime Minister 1763
props.caption: His math was brutally simple: colonies gained most from war and paid least — tax burden sat light next to English farmer even on same goods

points: Your taxes were a fraction of ours
Empire that protected you is sinking
Why should London drown in debt for empire colonists got on cheap?
Sent their sons, provided so many soldiers they fulfilled obligation
Then London mails bill with no vote attached
That's not math, that's a shakedown

props.title: Salutary Neglect — Named in 1775, Real for 100 Years Before
props.caption: Absentee customs officers, smuggled molasses, everybody rich enough not to ask questions — decades later Burke called it beneficial neglect

props.title: Debt Is the Engine
props.body: In 1763 neglect ended. Old laws got real teeth. On Grenville's desk already drafted: Sugar Act first big postwar tax and crackdown on smuggling everyone got rich on. Exam tip: when prompt asks why London turned to taxes, start with war debt. Smuggling makes colorful sentence. Debt is engine. Books say enormous — don't pin 140 million pounds figure you can't source. Box one done, but frontier already on fire.

highlights.note: Use books' word, not a number — don't pin 140M
First big postwar tax, gets own episode
AP thinking: war debt > smuggling anecdote

props.title: Burned Frontier, Empty Treasury
props.subline: Cheaper move: draw a line and freeze everyone east, or pour more soldiers west?

props.excerptText: We do hereby strictly forbid, on Pain of our Displeasure, all our loving Subjects from making any Purchases or Settlements whatever, or taking Possession of any of the Lands above reserved, without our especial Leave and Licence for that Purpose first obtained. And We do further declare it to be Our Royal Will and Pleasure to reserve under our Sovereignty, Protection, and Dominion, for the use of the said Indians, all the Lands and Territories not included within the Limits of Our said Three new Governments.
props.highlightedPhrase: a line along the crest of the Appalachians, and no colonial settlement past it
props.hippExplanation: Official reason buried in dry language: London didn't want another frontier war or cost of fighting one, wanted fur trade profits to keep flowing — second frontier war would cost more than empty treasury could bear. Triage, not revenge.

props.title: Triage, Not Punishment
props.caption: Not Britain punishing colonies 'no Ohio for you' — colonial read, wrong in useful way. Line was bandage on bleeding frontier, terrified of paying for second war

props.title: Fenced Off Fortunes
props.caption: Land speculators — men who bought western claims betting prices rise — including young George Washington speculating in western holdings. Settlers furious they'd fought for that land. Line didn't hold: already west and more coming. Came too late, stung as insult, failed as fence

props.title: A Real Fence. On Paper.
props.caption: Blue Ridge Parkway tunnels and mountains that never ended — on paper, a fence. Pattern: drawing line on map calling one side Indian country, America would copy trick later
props.prompt: Animate only the supplied still historical map with subtle environmental motion: faint drifting mist and slow-moving cloud shadows gliding over the Appalachian ridge, slight parchment texture shimmer, preserve the historical composition, add no people, text, or objects, and contain no camera movement.

points: Mississippi was the fence
Appalachians were the prize
Mississippi was the prize — vast new territory
Appalachians were the fence — Proclamation Line along crest

props.title: Purpose Before Grievance
props.body: Test tip: If stimulus hands you Proclamation's promise to leave Native lands undisturbed, ask what source is for. London dodging another expensive war. Purpose before grievance — that's how these sources crack open.

highlights.note: Stimulus language — ask purpose, not grievance
AP source skill: why London did it > how colonists felt

props.title: 10,000 Soldiers in America — Who Sleeps Best?
nodes: London leaves roughly 10,000 soldiers — three hear news: minister, settler, officer
Minister in London: frontier covered cheaply — sleeps okay. Officer: employed — sleeps best
Settler in Pennsylvania: hears boots in peacetime, does new math — officially to enforce line and keep burning frontier quiet
Colonist in Boston third answer: us — expensive army in peacetime looks like police for colonists

props.quote: The Proclamation Line of 1763, in one line: London draws a fence it can't patrol, to dodge a war it can't afford.

props.title: Pontiac's Rebellion — The Fire the Line Was Drawn Against
props.caption: Pontiac — like the car? Car company said it was. Ottawa chief around Great Lakes, not just a car name

points: Sat through ceremonies
Gave gifts — to Native nations gift-giving meant dominance and protection
It was diplomacy
Took French forts
General Amherst decided gift ceremonies demeaning and cut them off
No more gifts, no more diplomacy — just soldiers and settlers

props.title: Taking the Forts Cost Them the Room
props.caption: Message older than Pontiac: 1760-61 Delaware holy man Neolin preached apocalyptic vision — curb contact with fur traders, put down guns and alcohol, stop infighting or disappear

props.title: Fort After Fort — Deeply Organized
props.body: This wasn't random, it was organized. Deeply. Alliance struck fort after fort around Great Lakes, Detroit first then six more, settlements from upstate New York down Appalachian frontier. Several forts fell. Books count more than four hundred British soldiers and around two thousand colonists killed or captured. British handed out blankets deliberately infected with smallpox.

highlights.text: more than four hundred British soldiers and around two thousand colonists killed or captured

props.quote: One of the books calls it germ warfare, flatly.
props.byline: Marcus on smallpox blankets — Amherst replaced August 1763 by Thomas Gage, Gage broke rebellion, bloodshed into 1764

props.title: Mirror Image: The Paxton Boys
nodes: Scots-Irish frontiersmen in Pennsylvania decide guilty and innocent looked alike
1763 murder 20 peaceful Conestoga Indians, Christians with nothing to do with fighting
About 250 march on Philadelphia demanding colony stop protecting Indians
London gets message: frontier was tinderbox, every policy poured something on it — Proclamation was first pour

props.title: Sorting Rule: Who Rebelled in 1763?
props.body: Sorting rule test-ready: rebels in 1763 were Ottawa-led Native nations. If your draft says colonists rebelled, you've written wrong war.

props.title: Prophet vs War Chief — Don't Swap Jobs

points: Preached apocalyptic vision
Curb fur traders, put down guns and alcohol
Stop infighting or disappear
Around Great Lakes
Organized resistance, message still burning
First targets: forts

props.title: Box One Landed: End of Salutary Neglect
props.caption: War left London enormous debt — no number, books won't give one. Grenville did math, London started enforcing everything it used to ignore

props.title: Box Two Landed: Proclamation Line 1763
props.caption: Line along Appalachians no settlement past it — London dodging war pure triage. Fence held? No: failed as fence, came too late, stung as insult

props.title: Box Three Landed: Pontiac's Rebellion
props.caption: Pontiac Ottawa chief 1763 — Neolin was prophet. Forts fell, London panicked its way into whole new imperial policy

props.authorAndDate: British Crown, October 1763, in response to Pontiac's Rebellion
props.excerptText: That the several Nations or Tribes of Indians with whom We are connected, and who live under our Protection, should not be molested or disturbed in the Possession of such Parts of Our Dominions and Territories as are reserved to them as their Hunting Grounds.
props.highlightedPhrase: should not be molested or disturbed
props.hippExplanation: Proclamation was London's cheap answer to Pontiac's Rebellion outbreak — drawing settlement line through Appalachians. With treasury empty, freezing settlement west cost less than fighting another frontier war. Triage won because treasury empty.

props.title: Most Significant Effect? Broken Trust
props.body: Most significant effect of Seven Years' War — debt was policy problem later governments managed, territory stayed British, but broken trust never healed. Britain started treating colonies like problem to be managed, colonies started seeing Britain as threat to freedom. That's crack every later crisis widens.

highlights.note: Most significant — over debt or territory

props.title: What Changed After 1763 That Pushed Alliance to War?
nodes: British replace French diplomacy with soldiers
Amherst ends gift ceremonies French had used
Forts stop being trading partner's posts, become symbols of new order — first targets

props.title: Britain Won the War — and Couldn't Afford the Peace
props.subline: Next: taxes arrive — first sugar, then stamps, and fight over who gets to tax whom
